title: Youth organizations protest in Stockholm against militarization and living costs

tea.why: Protesters oppose military rearmament, privatization, climate change, and cuts to welfare, citing solidarity with European youth movements.
tea.want: They demand an end to militarization, privatization, and policies they argue negatively impact the future and living standards of young people.
tea.changed: Nov 20: A demonstration took place at Norra Bantorget in Stockholm as part of a coordinated international day of action.

summary: On November 20, 2026, various youth organizations held a demonstration at Norra Bantorget in Stockholm as part of a broader international initiative called International Youth Strike. The protest, which occurred despite snowy weather, was organized by groups including Revolutionär Kommunistisk Ungdom (RKU), Stockholm Academics for Palestine, Gatans Parlament, Ung Vänster, Förortsfeminister, and Ta tillbaka framtiden. Participants expressed opposition to military rearmament, privatization, the climate crisis, and welfare cuts. The event was part of a coordinated effort across approximately 25 countries to highlight issues affecting youth, such as the rising cost of living and global militarization. Speakers at the event emphasized themes of international solidarity and self-determination. No official response from government authorities was reported in the provided sources regarding the specific demands of the Stockholm demonstration.
response: No official response reported in the sources.

crowd.text: Flamman reported that at least one hundred youths were present in the park.

updates.text: A demonstration was held at Norra Bantorget in Stockholm as part of an international day of action.
